doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Long-term goals and songwriting
summary: She hopes to play certain places and projects, facing rejection, and mentions her tune 'You're the One I Think I've Waited For'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you have any long term goals?

There’s places I want to play and people I want to play with. You know I focus on it at different times. This is a quieter month for me so I’ll explore that again. I sense some — you know you’ve got to be prepared when you’re in this business for the rejection too. I might want to play at this place but they might not want to have me. So for whatever reason, too, there could be a million different reasons. So you may not even get an email back but you still keep trying. You’ve got to keep trying. So yeah, there’s a lot of stuff I still want to do. There’s a lot of projects I still want to do.
Write more songs, you’ve written some nice tunes.
I like that one you wrote “I Think You’re the One” —
“You’re The One I Think I’ve Waited For.”
Right. I like the “I think” in that title.
